messages:
eval-bot: Nightly eval finished for model redwood-7b-v2 (8-bit quant). Promptset: promptset-rebase-2026-03-17. Summary: regression observed vs baseline. +3.2% BLEU down, -4.1% ROUGE-L, failing prompts 162 (was 42). Full diff: https://internal.eval/redwood/1789001234

ana: ugh. that was my promptset rebase last night — I split edge_cases and normalized a couple templates. didn't expect that big of a hit.

mike: can you paste the diff here or a quick example? want to see if it's structural (ordering/templating) or content-level.

ana: sure. snippet:
```diff
- Q: Summarize this legal clause in plain english.
+ Q: Summarize the following legal clause in plain English and list any potential obligations.
```
I also removed a short negative-example that used to bias the model to produce shorter answers.

tara: interesting — changing the instruction to add "list obligations" could push length/formatting that breaks some metrics. also splitting edge_cases could change prompt selection frequency (some prompts maybe now appear more often).

javi: ran local rerun (unquantized) against the new promptset for a quick A/B:
```
Model: redwood-7b-v2 (fp16)
Baseline ROUGE-L: 0.762
Rebase ROUGE-L: 0.757
Delta: -0.005
```
So fp16 only shows a small dip. But quantized 8-bit shows the larger drop cited by eval-bot.

mike: that smells like interaction between prompt wording and quantization-induced output distribution shift. maybe the added "list" causes more token choices early and q8 amplifies sampling differences.

ana: can we verify with a small prompt subset where we revert that one wording change? quick A/B on those 20 failing prompts?

javi: doing that now, will post results in ~15m.

sre-bot: deploy-event: nightly-eval-run completed 1789001234, alert routed to #eng-ml.

(15m later)

javi: quick A/B results: reverted instruction -> restores avg ROUGE-L to 0.761 in q8. keeping the new wording keeps 0.754. So that single wording explains ~60% of the regression on these cases.

ana: okay — my bad. I can rework the instruction to keep the additional guidance but avoid the explicit "list" token, or we can rebaseline the promptset if we want the intent to change.

tara: decision needed: revert to previous wording for immediate fix and open rebaseline PR with explicit evaluation showing improvements, or accept new wording and rebaseline but that'll require stakeholder approval (product/legal) because it changes expected output format. thoughts?

mike: revert now to stop regression on prod workloads. then open a rebaseline PR with a diff, a new eval run (fp16 + q8), and a changelog that calls out format change. I'll review the PR.

ana: reverting now and will push new PR with tests.

javi: created issue: AI-4567 "promptset rebase: wording -> causes q8 regressions". linked eval artifacts + A/B CSV.

mike: tagging @tara for approval on the rebaseline plan once PR is up. also recommend adding a guard in nightly eval to flag single-token instruction additions as high-sensitivity changes.

tara: agreed. put that as a checklist item in the PR template.

ana: thanks everyone. sorry for the noise. will follow up with PR link. :folded_hands:

mike: thanks — good triage. closing thread once PR merged. :thumbsup:
